chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from al-Fuḍayl, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
Indeed, a man commits a sin, and so sustenance is warded off from him.
When they swore that they would surely cut its fruit in the morning, and they did not make any exception; so there came upon it a visitation from your Lord while they were asleep.

key_terms.الذَّنْبَ: the sin or act of disobedience
key_terms.لَيَصْرِمُنَّهَا: they would surely cut off its produce

ai.seo_question: Can sins cause a person’s sustenance to be withheld?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that sin can have worldly consequences, including the withholding of sustenance. Imam Abu Jaʿfar عليه السلام illustrates this meaning by reciting the verses about the أصحاب الجنة, whose wrongful intent led to the loss of their garden.
